steps.title: Why NumPy?
steps.body:
**NumPy** gives Python fast **n-dimensional arrays**. Operations apply to the whole array at once (**vectorized**), so you rarely write loops.

Every array has a **shape**, a **dtype** and supports slicing like lists but in many dimensions.

steps.title: Creating, indexing and slicing
steps.code:
import numpy as np

a = np.arange(1, 7).reshape(2, 3)
print(a)
print(a.shape)
print(a[1, 2])
print(a[:, 1])

notes.text: arange makes 1..6 and reshape turns it into 2 rows by 3 columns.
A colon means all rows; this takes column 1.

steps.title: Broadcasting and vector math
steps.code:
import numpy as np

v = np.array([1, 2, 3])
print(v * 2)
print(v + np.array([10, 20, 30]))
m = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
print(m + v)
print(np.dot(v, v))

notes.text: A scalar is broadcast to every element.
Arrays of the same shape combine element by element.
The 1-D vector is stretched across both rows.
dot multiplies pairs and adds them: 1+4+9.

steps.title: Linear algebra and statistics
steps.code:
import numpy as np

A = np.array([[2, 0], [0, 4]])
print(round(np.linalg.det(A), 2))
print(np.linalg.inv(A))
data = np.array([2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9])
print(data.mean(), data.std())
print(np.median(data))

notes.text: The determinant of a diagonal matrix is the product of its diagonal.
mean and std summarize the data.
The median is the middle value.

steps.title: Solving a linear system
steps.code:
import numpy as np

A = np.array([[3, 1], [1, 2]])
b = np.array([9, 8])
x = np.linalg.solve(A, b)
print(x.tolist())
print(np.allclose(A @ x, b))

notes.text: solve finds x so that A times x equals b.
@ is matrix multiplication; allclose checks the result.

steps.question: What does np.array([1, 2, 3]) * 2 give?
steps.explanation: NumPy multiplies every element, unlike a Python list which repeats.

steps.question: What is broadcasting?
options: Stretching smaller arrays to match shapes in an operation
steps.explanation: Broadcasting lets arrays of different shapes combine without copying data by hand.

examples.title: NumPy: Array Creation
examples.description: zeros, ones, arange, linspace and eye.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

print(np.zeros(3))
print(np.ones((2, 2)))
print(np.arange(0, 10, 3))
print(np.linspace(0, 1, 5))
print(np.eye(3))

examples.title: NumPy: Indexing & Slicing
examples.description: Read elements, rows, columns and masks.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

a = np.arange(1, 13).reshape(3, 4)
print(a)
print(a[0, 1], a[-1, -1])
print(a[1])
print(a[:, 2])
print(a[1:, :2])
print(a[a % 2 == 0])

examples.title: NumPy: Broadcasting
examples.code:
import numpy as np

col = np.array([[1], [2], [3]])
row = np.array([10, 20, 30])
print(col + row)
print(col * 2)
print(row / 10)

examples.title: NumPy: Vector Math
examples.description: Dot product, norm and cumulative sums.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

a = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 2.0])
b = np.array([3.0, 0.0, 4.0])
print(a + b)
print(a * b)
print(np.dot(a, b))
print(np.linalg.norm(a))
print(np.cumsum(a))
print(np.sqrt(b))

examples.title: NumPy: Linear Algebra
examples.description: Matrix product, determinant, inverse and solve.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

A = np.array([[4.0, 3.0], [6.0, 3.0]])
B = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 2.0]])
print(A @ B)
print(round(np.linalg.det(A), 2))
print(np.linalg.inv(A).round(3))
print(np.linalg.solve(A, np.array([10.0, 12.0])))
print(A.T)

examples.title: NumPy: Statistics
examples.code:
import numpy as np

x = np.array([2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9])
print(x.mean(), x.std(), x.var())
print(np.median(x), x.min(), x.max())
print(np.percentile(x, [25, 75]))
y = 2 * x + 1
print(round(np.corrcoef(x, y)[0, 1], 3))
